title: PR workflow
lede: How one task becomes one merged PR: local gates first, real checks on GitHub, and a merge only the owner authorizes.

branch.name: Branch
branch.role: Pull the latest main and cut a fresh branch for one independent task.
details: One task per PR and merge cycle.

local.name: Local gates
local.role: Run the integration tests and make ci before opening anything.
details: Start from a clean tree with commits ahead of main.

more: Still red: failing integration tests stop with no PR; a red make ci opens the PR as a DRAFT listing the red gates.

details: Then bump the version and push.

open.name: Open the PR
open.role: /create-pr opens the PR with a structured body and starts watching its checks.
details: /simplify must score every changed file 10/10, or approved overrides cover the rest, before the PR opens.
The body has a Summary, Critical changes, gate status, Quality Scores, a Test plan and the session URL.
Subscribe to the PR, or run gh pr checks --watch.

checks.name: Verify checks
checks.role: Read the actual check conclusions on the final head, not the merge button.
details: First remove the handoff file, push, and run check-handoff --pre-merge, so the final CI run judges the cleared head.
Capture the watch command's own exit code.
The Security scan check must pass.
risks: GitHub counts a skipped required check as passing; treat a skip as suspect.
qs: Why isn't a green merge button enough?

merge.name: Authorized merge
merge.role: With the owner's explicit authorization, the orchestrator squash-merges it onto main as one commit.
details: The squash merge uses --match-head-commit, so only the commit whose checks were read can land.
Confirm the PR is MERGED, pull main, and cut a fresh branch before the next task.

makeci.d: The local pre-merge gate: unit and heavy integration checks.

critical.d: Up to five path:line notes of what changed and what depends on it.

squash.d: One PR lands as one commit on main.

ask.context: The reader wants to understand how scaffold's agents take a task from branch to a merged PR safely.
